`user.id === user.id` has the same answer every time, so the condition around it tests nothing. It is almost always a typo for a comparison with another value.

The rule looks at `==`, `===`, `!=`, `!==`, `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`, and reports when both sides are written the same way.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function isSameUser(user, other) {
  return user.id === user.id;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function isSameUser(user, other) {
  return user.id === other.id;
}
```

`value !== value` is `true` only for `NaN`. It is reported too. Say what you mean instead:

{/* bad */}
```js
if (price !== price) {
  price = 0;
}
```

{/* good */}
```js
if (Number.isNaN(price)) {
  price = 0;
}
```
